A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 16-page versions of the same DiagramQG/HKI-DQG study, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies can be identified directly and do not constitute missing evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiagramQG evaluations, natural-image benchmark results, parameter sensitivity experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports OK-VQA/A-OKVQA evaluations and qualitative comparisons with GPT-4o.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same HierKnowExtract, KnowSelect, and KnowFusionQG pipeline, frozen knowledge-extraction VLM, patch selection, attention, and gated fusion. Equations 1–7 and the architecture are unchanged; abbreviated model names do not identify new components.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the OK-VQA and A-OKVQA natural-image question-generation datasets in Table 4, substantially expanding the evaluated data coverage. DiagramQG, VQG-COCO, and K-VQG remain; DiagramQG's subjects, concepts, and reported overall counts are unchanged.

E2.justification: LV2-Net becomes an evaluated comparator on the added benchmarks, and Figure 8 introduces qualitative comparisons with GPT-4o. Existing DiagramQG and retained natural-image comparator sets are preserved. MDN's appearance in the main VQG-COCO table is a relocation of a comparison already present in v1 Appendix D.

E3.justification: v1 Appendices B–C specify a 70:10:20 training/validation/test split. New Section 5.2 in v2 instead specifies 70:5:25, a substantive reported change to the central benchmark's evaluation partition. However, v2 retains the old appendix split and counts, leaving the actual partition and whether experiments were rerun unresolved.

E4.justification: Figure 8 and the main case study change from four HKI-DQG examples to two comparisons against GPT-4o, including a new filter-feeding example that examines concept relevance. The parameter sensitivity experiment and Appendix E's failure cases and knowledge analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run/seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the model comparisons. Figure 7 retains the same across-concept mean display. More emphatic wording in v2 does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds complete OK-VQA/A-OKVQA result comparisons: HKI-DQGQ reports BLEU-1 of 33.24/34.57, below IM-VQG's 36.47/39.30. Figure 8 adds outputs and changes the bivalve prediction from Small Planktivorous Fish to Sea Ducks. Table 2 and sensitivity scores remain identical. Retained natural-image numbers appear under exchanged CIDEr/METEOR headings in v2's main tables, conflicting with Appendix D; these cannot be interpreted as performance changes.

T1.justification: The conditional generation problem, mathematical architecture in Equations 1–7, and DEHN definition are retained. Neither version adds or removes theoretical propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the claimed state-of-the-art natural-image evaluation from two datasets to four, and the introduction explicitly includes this broader validation among the contributions. The central claims about DiagramQG's novelty and HKI-DQG as an adaptable baseline remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded benchmark results as evidence of better semantic and contextual question generation. Its main case study now emphasizes concept relevance relative to GPT-4o, replacing the main-text failure-focused discussion. The substantive limitations concerning constraint loss, diagram interpretation, and concept ambiguity remain in Appendix E.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the documented Google Image Search source with Hugging Face, GitHub, and Roboflow, adding licenses and source percentages. v2 also documents diagram/question non-overlap and concept coverage. Conversely, it removes v1's dataset/code link and the separate-reviewer and five-point grading details. Most implementation information is retained; link removal does not establish resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same cited works and the same VQG/DQA research framing. LV2-Net's source [20] and MDN [30] were already cited in v1. Related-work wording changes do not substantively revise novelty or relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, rewrites the main case study, adds a Split subsection with subsequent renumbering, and adds two authors and affiliations. The overall organization, method exposition, and nearly all supplementary text remain intact.

P2.justification: The combined natural-image table becomes separate K-VQG and multi-dataset tables. Figure 8 is redrawn from four full-width examples into two single-column comparisons, and Table 2 is compacted with abbreviated names. The sensitivity header changes from DERN to DEHN. Most figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmarks and provenance information are useful, but v2 introduces conflicting evaluation splits and exchanges CIDEr/METEOR headings for retained results while its appendix preserves the original assignments. Removing the dataset/code link also reduces actionable reproducibility information. These reporting problems outweigh the benefit of broader validation, producing a limited overall decline in reliability while the core method, main results, and appendix analyses remain intact.
